facts.statement: The genus Procaimanoidea was named in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore after his death.
facts.quote: It was named posthumously in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore

facts.statement: The type species P. utahensis was found in the middle Eocene Uintan formation of Utah.
facts.quote: the type species is P. utahensis, from the Uintan (middle Eocene) of Utah

facts.statement: The description of Procaimanoidea relies on fossil USNM 15996, which includes a nearly complete skull and a partial left hind leg.
facts.quote: It is based on USNM 15996, a nearly complete skull and partial left hind leg

facts.statement: The species P. kayi was originally named in 1941 by C.C. Mook from early Eocene remains in Wyoming before being reassigned to Procaimanoidea.
facts.quote: A second species, P. kayi, was named in 1941 by C.C. Mook as a species of Hassiacosuchus, for remains from the Bridgerian (early Eocene) of Wyoming

facts.statement: Wassersug and Hecht reassigned the species P. kayi to the genus Procaimanoidea in 1967.
facts.quote: It was reassigned to Procaimanoidea in 1967 by Wassersug and Hecht

facts.statement: Procaimanoidea was a small alligatorid with slightly heterodont dentition where the last four teeth on each jaw side had blunt tips.
facts.quote: Procaimanoidea was a small alligatorid, and slightly heterodont, the last four teeth on each side of the jaws having blunt tips

facts.statement: Recent studies consistently classify Procaimanoidea within the subfamily Alligatorinae, though its exact position within the group remains disputed.
facts.quote: Recent studies have consistently resolved Procaimanoidea as a member of Alligatorinae, although its relative placement is disputed

facts.statement: The fossil record for Procaimanoidea spans from the Maastrichtian to the Bartonian stages, between 72.2 and 39.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Bartonian (72.2 to 39.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Procaimanoidea lived during the Eocene epoch in North America.
rejected.quote: Procaimanoidea... is an extinct genus of alligatorid from the Eocene of North America
